title: Overnight Oats with Berries
summary: Make-ahead oats that are ready when you wake up.
ingredients: 1 cup nonfat milk or unsweetened almond milk
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, chia seeds and honey together in a jar or bowl.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, or at least 4 hours.
Stir, top with berries and serve cold.
notes: Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 days.
heartNotes: Oats are a good source of soluble fiber, and the berries bring most of the sweetness, so a teaspoon of honey is plenty. Use nonfat or low-fat milk and plain nonfat Greek yogurt to keep saturated fat low.

title: Potato Shakshuka
summary: Smoky tomato and potato skillet with eggs baked right in.
ingredients: 1 pound baby Yukon gold potatoes, halved
1 jar (12 oz) roasted red peppers, rinsed, drained and chopped
2 cups baby spinach or chopped kale
1/4 cup fresh parsley, roughly chopped, for garnish
2 tablespoons toasted sesame seeds, for garnish
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and potatoes until softened, 8 to 10 minutes. Stir in the chipotle powder, smoked paprika and a pinch of pepper for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, red peppers and 1/3 cup water. Bring to a low boil, then simmer over medium heat until the sauce thickens and the potatoes are fork-tender, about 5 minutes. Season with pepper.

Stir in the spinach or kale until it wilts. Make 4 to 6 wells in the sauce, sprinkle a little cheese into each if using, and crack an egg into each one. Cover and cook until the whites are set and the yolks are done the way you like them.
Top with parsley and sesame seeds and serve with whole-grain bread.
heartNotes: Lightened: no added salt, low-sodium tomatoes, avocado oil, less cheese (reduced-fat and optional), and a couple of cups of greens. Eggs fit a heart-healthy diet in moderation; for less cholesterol, use 4 eggs instead of 6.

title: Black Bean and Corn Salad
summary: A bright, filling salad that holds up well in the fridge.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) low-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
1 1/2 cups corn (frozen and thawed, or fresh)
steps: Combine the beans, corn, bell pepper, tomatoes, onion, jalapeño and parsley in a large bowl.
Whisk the avocado oil, lime juice and cumin together.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss. Chill 20 minutes before serving if you have time.
notes: Add diced avocado right before serving.
heartNotes: Choose low-sodium beans, or rinse regular canned beans well to wash away some of the sodium. Beans and vegetables add fiber, and avocado oil keeps the fat unsaturated.

title: Hummus Veggie Wraps
summary: A crunchy, no-cook wrap you can make in five minutes.
ingredients: 1/4 cup roasted red peppers, rinsed and sliced
steps: Spread hummus over each tortilla, leaving a small border.
Layer the spinach, cucumber, carrot, cabbage and red peppers down the center.
Roll up tightly, folding in the sides, and cut in half.
notes: Wrap in foil to pack for the road or the arena.
heartNotes: Look for a low-sodium hummus, or make your own without salt. Whole-wheat tortillas add fiber.

title: Jalisco Style Ceviche
summary: Fresh, zesty shrimp ceviche with crunchy vegetables.
ingredients: 1.3 pounds shrimp (or fish), cut into 1/2 inch cubes
Juice of several limes, enough to cover the shrimp, about 10-15
1 serrano pepper, chopped, or more to add heat
steps: Blanch the shrimp or fish in boiling water for 3 minutes. Immediately submerge in ice bath to stop cooking process.
Drain and submerge shrimp in lime juice.
Refrigerate for 2 hours.
Drain, then mix with all the remaining ingredients.
notes: Serve with a little diced avocado for healthy fat.
heartNotes: Shrimp is very low in saturated fat. Rinse the capers to wash off some of their salt, and skip any added salt; the lime does the work.

title: Lemon Herb Baked Salmon
summary: Salmon roasted with lemon, garlic and dill on one pan with asparagus and tomatoes.
ingredients: 1 tbsp fresh dill, chopped (or 1 tsp dried)
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.

Toss the asparagus and tomatoes with half the avocado oil and spread them on the sheet. Nestle the salmon in among the vegetables, brush it with the rest of the oil, and sprinkle with garlic, lemon zest, dill and pepper.
Lay lemon slices on top and bake 12–15 minutes, until the fish flakes easily with a fork.
notes: Serve with brown rice.
heartNotes: Salmon is a fatty fish rich in omega-3s. Lemon, garlic and dill carry the flavor, so there's no salt in this recipe.

title: Lemon Cod and Orzo Skillet
summary: Golden seared cod over lemony orzo and asparagus, all in one skillet.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon extra-virgin olive oil (for the lemons)
1 Meyer or regular lemon, sliced, plus more for serving
1 bunch asparagus, ends trimmed, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 cup uncooked orzo (whole-wheat if you can find it)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh dill, for serving
steps: Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Season the cod with pepper and dust both sides with flour. Sear until golden, 3 to 4 minutes per side, then move to a plate.
Add the remaining tablespoon of oil and sear the lemon slices until golden, about 1 minute per side. Add them to the plate with the cod.

Add the garlic, asparagus and orzo to the skillet and toast for 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in the broth and lemon juice, bring to a boil, and cook, stirring now and then, until the orzo is al dente, about 10 minutes. Stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Set the cod and lemon slices back on top to warm through. Finish with dill and extra lemon.
heartNotes: Lightened: olive oil replaces the salted butter and there's no added salt. Cod is a lean fish, low-sodium broth keeps the orzo in check, and asparagus and spinach add greens.

title: Roasted Vegetable Quinoa Bowl
summary: Quinoa topped with roasted vegetables and a lemon-tahini drizzle.
ingredients: 2 cups water or low-sodium vegetable broth
1 can (15 oz) low-sodium chickpeas, rinsed and drained
2 cups baby kale or spinach, for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sweet potato, zucchini, onion, bell pepper and chickpeas with avocado oil on a baking sheet.
Roast 25–30 minutes, turning once, until the vegetables are tender and browned.
Meanwhile, simmer the quinoa in the water or broth, covered, for 15 minutes. Let it rest 5 minutes, then fluff.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice and water into a pourable sauce.
Divide the greens and quinoa into bowls, top with the vegetables and drizzle with the sauce.
notes: Packs well for lunches through the week.
heartNotes: Plant protein from chickpeas and quinoa, healthy fats from avocado oil and tahini, a bowl full of vegetables, and no added salt.

title: Turkey and Vegetable Chili
summary: A hearty one-pot chili with lean turkey and plenty of vegetables.
ingredients: 2 cans (15 oz each) low-sodium kidney beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Brown the turkey, breaking it up, about 6 minutes.
Add the onion, bell pepper, carrots, zucchini and garlic. Cook 5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the chili powder and cumin for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, beans and broth. Simmer, partly covered, for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
notes: Freezes well for up to 3 months.
heartNotes: Lean ground turkey, low-sodium tomatoes and beans, and low-sodium broth keep this chili heart-friendly, and the extra vegetables add fiber.

title: Seasoned Taco Meat
summary: Flavorful taco meat without the filler and sodium of seasoning pouches.
replaces: Taco meat made with seasoning packets
ingredients: 1 lb 93% lean ground beef or lean ground turkey
1 small zucchini or 1 bell pepper, very finely diced
steps: Brown the meat in a lightly oiled deep pan, breaking it into very fine pieces. Drain off any fat.
Cook until all the liquid has evaporated.
Add the onion, garlic and zucchini or pepper and sweat for 3 to 4 minutes, then add all the spices and cook until fragrant.
Add the stock, tomato sauce, sweetener and vinegar.
Bring to a simmer, then reduce over low heat for 15 to 20 minutes.
notes: The finely diced vegetables disappear into the meat and stretch it further. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend.
heartNotes: Use 93% lean ground beef or lean ground turkey, low-sodium stock and low-sodium tomato sauce, and drain any fat after browning. The brown sugar is swapped for a little optional monk fruit, and hidden vegetables stretch the meat.

title: Cowboy Butter Air Fryer Chicken
summary: Skinless chicken marinated in a lightened-up, herby cowboy butter, then air fried.
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts
steps: Mix everything except the chicken to make the cowboy butter. Set some aside to spread on bread or sandwiches.
Coat the chicken thighs in the cowboy butter and marinate for 1 hour, or overnight.
Air fry at 385°F for 16 minutes, flipping halfway, until the chicken reaches 165°F inside.
notes: Serve with roasted vegetables or a big salad.
heartNotes: Lightened: made with light mayonnaise instead of butter, skinless chicken, and no added salt. Worcestershire and Dijon add sodium, so use low-sodium versions if you can find them.

title: Garlic Roasted Green Beans
summary: Crisp-tender green beans with garlic and lemon.
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F.
Toss the green beans with avocado oil, garlic and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast 12–15 minutes, until tender and lightly browned. Sprinkle with lemon zest.
heartNotes: No salt needed. Garlic and lemon zest bring the flavor.

title: Calabacitas
summary: A cheesy Southwest sauté of summer squash, corn, tomatoes and peppers.
ingredients: 1 jalapeño pepper, diced (seeds removed if you don't want it spicy)
1 can (15 oz) whole kernel corn, drained
1 large zucchini, sliced into half moons
1 large yellow squash, sliced into half moons
steps: Heat the oil in a large skillet. Cook the onion and peppers for 5 minutes.
Add the corn and tomatoes and cook 5 minutes.
Add the squash, garlic and seasonings and cook 5 minutes.
Add the water, cover and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the cheddar and milk until melted. Top with parsley if you like.
heartNotes: Lightened from the original: the salt is cut from 2 teaspoons to an optional pinch, with reduced-fat cheese and low-fat milk. The cumin, oregano and peppers carry plenty of flavor.

title: No-Salt Taco and Fajita Seasoning
summary: All the flavor of a taco packet with none of the added salt.
steps: Mix everything together and store in an airtight container.
heartNotes: Taco packets can carry a lot of sodium per serving. This blend gets its flavor from chiles and spices instead, with zero added salt.

title: Salt-Free Creole Seasoning
summary: A smoky, peppery Creole blend with all the flavor and none of the salt.
steps: Mix everything together and store in an airtight container.
heartNotes: Many store-bought Creole blends list salt as the first ingredient. This version leaves it out completely.

title: Salt-Free Burger Seasoning
summary: An all-purpose, salt-free blend to mix into patties or sprinkle on top.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, for extra heat)
steps: Mix everything together in a small bowl until evenly combined.
Store in an airtight container.
heartNotes: Salt-free. Great on lean beef, turkey or veggie burgers. If you miss the salt, a squeeze of lemon or a splash of vinegar brightens the flavor.

title: Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute
summary: A homemade stand-in for soy sauce with a fraction of the salt.
ingredients: 1 cup low-sodium beef or vegetable broth
1 teaspoon molasses (for color and depth), or 2 teaspoons golden monk fruit sweetener
steps: Whisk everything together in a pot and bring to a boil. Boil for 1 minute.
Lower the heat to medium and cook for 10 minutes more. Remove from the heat and let cool.
notes: Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend. Adapted from Sans Salt (sans-salt.com).
heartNotes: Uses only 1/8 teaspoon of salt for the whole cup. Use it anywhere you'd use soy sauce, plus in place of fish, hoisin, oyster or teriyaki sauce.

title: Healthy BBQ Sauce
summary: A low-sodium barbecue sauce with a splash of bourbon.
steps: In a large pot over medium heat, cook the onion, bell pepper, garlic, apple juice concentrate and vinegar.
Cook until it turns syrupy, about 8 to 10 minutes.
Add everything else. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer for 1 hour.
heartNotes: Low-sodium tomato puree and chili powder keep the sodium low, and there's no added fat. It uses half the usual apple juice concentrate, so it's lower in sugar than bottled sauce.

title: Red Sauce
summary: A quick, mildly spicy red sauce for enchiladas and more.
steps: Add everything to a small saucepan and bring to a boil.
Turn the heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
heartNotes: Canned enchilada sauce is often high in sodium. Using low-sodium tomato sauce keeps this version very low.

title: Canned Tomato Salsa
summary: A big-batch salsa for water-bath canning. Makes 16 to 18 pints.
ingredients: 7 quarts peeled, cored, chopped paste or plum tomatoes
4 cups seeded, chopped long green chiles
1/2 cup seeded, finely chopped jalapeño peppers
2 cups bottled lemon or lime juice
steps: Wear gloves when handling the hot peppers, and keep your hands away from your face.

If you want to peel the long green chiles, slit each one, blister the skins under a broiler or in a 400°F oven for 6 to 8 minutes, cover with a damp cloth to steam, then peel. Seed and chop. Jalapeños don't need peeling.
Dip the tomatoes in boiling water for 30 to 60 seconds until the skins split, then into cold water. Slip off the skins and remove the cores.

Combine everything except the oregano, cumin and parsley in a large pot. Bring to a boil, stirring often, then simmer for 10 minutes. Add the optional spices and simmer 20 minutes more, stirring now and then.
Ladle hot salsa into hot jars, leaving 1/2-inch headspace. Remove air bubbles, wipe the rims and put on the lids.
Process pints in a boiling-water canner for 15 minutes.
notes: Paste tomatoes work best; slicing tomatoes take much longer to cook down. Keep the ingredient amounts as written so the salsa stays safely acidic for canning, and add processing time if you're at a high altitude.
heartNotes: Salt is here for flavor only; the bottled lemon or lime juice is what keeps it safe to can. Leave the salt out or cut it way down for a low-sodium salsa.

title: Chipotle Honey Vinaigrette
summary: Smoky, sweet and tangy dressing made in the blender.
steps: Blend everything together until smooth.
heartNotes: Uses salt substitute instead of salt, and avocado oil, which is low in saturated fat. Start with less honey and add to taste. Chipotles in adobo do contain some sodium, so taste before adding more.

title: Spicy Peanut Sauce
summary: A sweet-and-spicy peanut dressing for noodles, salads and bowls.
ingredients: 1/4 cup natural creamy peanut butter (no salt or sugar added)
1 1/2–2 tablespoons water, depending on preferred thickness
1 tablespoon Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or reduced-sodium soy sauce
steps: Whisk everything together until smooth, adding water until it's as thick or thin as you like.
heartNotes: Natural peanut butter and the homemade soy sauce substitute cut the salt, and a tablespoon of honey replaces the maple syrup. Peanut butter's fat is mostly unsaturated, but a little goes a long way.

title: Lighter Tartar Sauce
summary: A tangy, lighter tartar sauce made with Greek yogurt.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon capers, rinsed and finely chopped
1/4 cup dill pickle relish (low-sodium if available)
steps: Mix everything together well.
Refrigerate for a day before serving so the flavors come together.
heartNotes: Lightened: half the mayonnaise is swapped for nonfat Greek yogurt and the mayo is light, cutting fat and saturated fat.

title: Yogurt Garlic Chicken Marinade
summary: A tangy yogurt-and-garlic marinade that keeps lean chicken juicy.
steps: Whisk all the ingredients together.
Coat skinless chicken (breasts, tenders or skinless wings) and marinate 1 to 2 hours, then bake, grill or air fry.
heartNotes: Lightened from Ryan's wing marinade: no added salt, less oil (avocado oil), nonfat dairy, and made for skinless chicken, since most of a wing's saturated fat is in the skin.

title: Cranberry Sauce
summary: Homemade cranberry sauce loaded with fruit, pecans and warm spices.
ingredients: 1/2 to 2/3 cup monk fruit sweetener, to taste
steps: Bring the water to a boil, then stir in the monk fruit sweetener until it dissolves.
Lower the heat to a simmer and add everything else.
Cover and simmer for 30 minutes, or until the cranberries burst. Let cool.
notes: Great spooned over plain nonfat Greek yogurt or oatmeal. Cranberries are very tart, so taste near the end and add a little more sweetener if needed. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend.
heartNotes: No salt and no fat added. The cup of sugar is replaced with monk fruit, the dried fruit is unsweetened and optional, and the orange, apple and pear bring natural sweetness.

title: Baked Cinnamon Apples
summary: Warm apples with oats and cinnamon, no added butter.
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F.
Toss the apples with cinnamon and honey and spread in a small baking dish.
Sprinkle with oats and walnuts.
Bake 25–30 minutes, until the apples are soft.
notes: Top with a spoonful of plain Greek yogurt.
heartNotes: A naturally sweet dessert with fiber from the apples and oats, no butter, and just a drizzle of honey.

title: Mahi Mahi with Tomato Lemon Sauce
summary: Golden seared mahi mahi in a quick blistered-tomato, lemon and basil pan sauce.
steps: Pat the fillets dry and season both sides with the pepper and garlic powder.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the fish without moving it until golden, about 3 minutes, then flip and cook about 3 minutes more. Move the fish to a plate.
Add the tomatoes to the same pan and cook until they start to blister, about 4 minutes. Stir in the shallots and garlic and cook about 1 minute, until fragrant.
Pour in the broth, vinegar and lemon juice. Simmer about 4 minutes, until the tomatoes slump into a sauce. Stir in the spinach until it wilts, then the lemon zest and basil.
Return the fish to the pan and spoon the sauce over the top to serve.
notes: Adapted from Every Last Bite (everylastbite.com).
heartNotes: Lightened: olive oil replaces the butter, the added salt is gone, and the broth is low-sodium. Garlic powder, lemon and vinegar carry the flavor, and spinach adds greens. Mahi mahi is a lean, low-fat fish.

title: Chili Garlic Shrimp Pasta
summary: One-pan spaghetti cooked right in a garlicky chili sauce, finished with shrimp and lime.
ingredients: 1/2 to 1 teaspoon red pepper flakes (or 1 teaspoon chili crisp)
1 tablespoon Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or reduced-sodium soy sauce
1 lime, half sliced and half in wedges
steps: Warm the avocado oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and stir for 15 to 20 seconds, just until fragrant.
Stir in the soy sauce substitute, rice vinegar, sweetener and 2 cups of water.
Turn the heat to high, add the dry spaghetti and bring to a simmer, turning the noodles as they soften.
Keep stirring as the liquid reduces and turns glossy from the pasta starch. Add more water about 1/2 cup at a time only if the noodles need it.

When the liquid has reduced by about half, add the broccoli and cook 2 minutes. Add the shrimp and lime slices and cook just until the shrimp turn pink, 2 to 3 minutes, then fold in the spinach until it wilts.
Top with scallions and serve with lime wedges.
notes: Keep the sauce a little loose; it thickens fast as it sits. Adapted from Chef Fatty (cheffatty.com). Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend.
heartNotes: Lightened: the original's teaspoon of salt and the fish sauce are gone, avocado oil replaces the butter, and a homemade or reduced-sodium soy sauce stands in for regular. Chili crisp is salty, so red pepper flakes are the default. Whole-wheat pasta, broccoli and spinach add fiber.

title: Spicy Bulgogi (Pork, Beef or Chicken)
summary: Sweet, spicy, garlicky Korean-style bulgogi built on a low-sodium sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb pork tenderloin, flank steak or boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into 1/4-inch strips
2 tablespoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site) or coconut aminos
steps: Stir together the soy sauce substitute, sesame oil, sweetener, sherry vinegar, garlic, ginger, gochugaru and hot sauce. Leave out the balsamic for now.
Heat a little of the oil in a cast-iron or heavy skillet and cook the onion, bell pepper and carrots until just soft. Move them to a plate.

Add a little more oil and sear the meat in small batches in a single layer, leaving each batch alone for about 2 minutes so it browns. Add each batch to the vegetables. Lean cuts cook fast, so keep the strips thin.
Return the meat and vegetables to the hot pan over high heat, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 to 2 minutes, until it thickens slightly. Turn off the heat.
Once it stops bubbling, stir in the balsamic vinegar. Top with scallions and sesame seeds.
notes: Serve over brown rice or wrapped in lettuce leaves. To make it mild, skip the gochugaru and hot sauce. Adapted from Sans Salt (sans-salt.com). Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend.
heartNotes: Already low in sodium thanks to the homemade soy sauce substitute. Lightened further: lean pork tenderloin, flank steak or chicken breast replaces fatty pork shoulder, monk fruit replaces the brown sugar, and peppers and carrots add vegetables.

title: Ginger Scallion Oil
summary: A sizzling, fragrant ginger and scallion oil to spoon over rice, noodles, fish or chicken.
steps: Peel the ginger with the edge of a spoon and mince it finely. Finely chop the scallions. Chop them almost to a paste for a smooth sauce, or leave them coarser for texture. Put both in a heatproof bowl.
Warm the oil in a small saucepan over medium heat until tiny bubbles rise from the bottom. Take it off the heat.
Carefully pour the hot oil over the ginger and scallions. It will sizzle.
Let it cool for at least 5 minutes, then stir in the rice vinegar if using and stir again before serving.
notes: For heat, add dried chilies or Sichuan peppercorns to the bowl before the hot oil. Keeps up to 2 weeks in a sealed jar in the fridge. Adapted from Phase Change Kitchen (phasechangeskitchen.com).
heartNotes: Lightened: the salt is now an optional pinch, and a splash of rice vinegar brightens it instead. Avocado oil is mostly unsaturated fat. It's still oil, so a spoonful goes a long way.

title: Thai Coconut Shrimp Curry
summary: A creamy red curry with shrimp, peppers and jalapeño, ready in 30 minutes.
ingredients: 1 lb raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 cup snap peas or chopped broccoli
1 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 1 1/2 tablespoons cold water
Juice of 1 lime, plus wedges for serving
steps: Heat the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Cook the onion, bell pepper, snap peas and jalapeño until just softened, 4 to 5 minutes. Lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Lower the heat to medium. Whisk in the coconut milk, curry paste and sweetener and bring to a gentle boil.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and simmer about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened.
Pat the shrimp dry and add them to the sauce with the vegetables. Simmer gently just until the shrimp are pink and opaque, then stir in the spinach until it wilts.
Stir in the lime juice, taste, and add red pepper flakes for more heat. Top with Thai basil and serve with brown rice and lime wedges.
notes: Leave the jalapeño seeds in for more heat, or take them out for a milder curry. Adapted from Peas and Crayons (peasandcrayons.com). Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend.
heartNotes: Lightened: light coconut milk replaces full-fat, which cuts the saturated fat by more than half. The fish sauce is gone, there's less curry paste (it's salty), monk fruit replaces the brown sugar, and lime makes up the difference. Extra vegetables stretch each serving.

title: Southwest Chicken Salad
summary: Smoky, spicy shredded chicken tossed with beans, corn and fresh vegetables in a creamy Greek yogurt dressing.
ingredients: 500 g (about 1.1 lb) boneless, skinless chicken breast
100 g (about 2/3 cup) low-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
125 g (about 1/2 cup) plain nonfat Greek yogurt
1 teaspoon honey or monk fruit sweetener
steps: Season the chicken breast on all sides with the paprika, cayenne, onion powder and garlic powder.
Air fry at 360°F for 22 minutes, flipping halfway through, until the chicken reaches 165°F inside.
Let the chicken rest for 10 minutes, then shred it into thin pieces with two forks.
Whisk all the dressing ingredients together until smooth.
In a large bowl, combine the shredded chicken, bell pepper, onion, corn, tomato, black beans, parsley and lime juice. Add the dressing and mix well.
notes: Keeps well in the fridge for 3 to 4 days, so it's great for meal prep. Serve it on its own, over greens, or in lettuce wraps. Using 2 teaspoons of cayenne makes it spicy; use half if you want it milder. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend.
heartNotes: No added salt: the spice blend, lime and parsley carry the flavor. Lean chicken breast, nonfat Greek yogurt and just a little light mayo keep the saturated fat low, and the beans add fiber.

title: Hot and Sour Chicken Soup
summary: A tangy, peppery chicken soup loaded with vegetables, with far less salt than takeout.
ingredients: 300 g (about 2/3 lb) boneless, skinless chicken breast, boiled and shredded
1 cup sliced mushrooms (shiitake are great here)
1 cup carrots, cut into thin strips
2 tablespoons reduced-sodium soy sauce, or 1/4 cup Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site)
3 tablespoons rice vinegar or Chinkiang black vinegar, plus more to taste
1 teaspoon honey or monk fruit sweetener
3 tablespoons cornstarch mixed with 1/2 cup cold water
1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil (optional, to finish)
steps: Heat the avocado oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the garlic and ginger for about 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the shredded chicken, mushrooms and pepper and cook for a few minutes, until the mushrooms soften.
Stir in the cabbage, corn, carrots, soy sauce, red pepper flakes, garlic powder, vinegar and sweetener. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes.
Pour in the broth and water, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Uncover and stir in the cornstarch slurry. Simmer, stirring, until the soup thickens slightly.
While stirring the soup in a slow circle, drizzle in the beaten eggs so they form thin ribbons.
Taste and add a splash more vinegar if you want it more sour. Top with scallions and a few drops of sesame oil, and serve hot.
notes: Keeps 4 days in the fridge; the eggs are best added fresh if you plan to reheat a big batch. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend. Adapted from GJ's Sweets & Savoury (Facebook).
heartNotes: Lightened: no added salt or bouillon cube, low-sodium broth instead, half the soy sauce, and no oyster sauce. One tablespoon of oil replaces four, sugar drops from a tablespoon to a teaspoon, and egg whites stand in for one of the yolks. Extra vinegar, ginger, white pepper and red pepper flakes keep the hot-and-sour punch.

title: Posole Rojo
summary: Ryan's red chile posole: slow-simmered lean pork tenderloin and hominy in a deep, smoky chile broth.
ingredients: 2 lb pork tenderloin, trimmed of all visible fat and cut in half
3 cans (15 oz each) white hominy, drained and rinsed well
Potassium chloride salt substitute, a pinch to taste (optional)
Dried oregano, crumbled between your fingers
steps: Break the stems off the chiles de árbol and anchos and shake out as many seeds as you can. Put the chiles in a bowl, cover with boiling water, and weigh them down with a plate. Soak until soft, about 30 minutes.
Move the chiles and 1 1/2 cups of the soaking liquid to a blender, add the smashed garlic, and blend until smooth. Push the sauce through a fine-mesh strainer with a spatula and discard the solids.
Rub the pork all over with the cumin. Heat the avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat and cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes. Add the chopped garlic and cook 2 minutes.
Turn the heat to medium-high. Push the onion and garlic to one side and sear the pork on the other side, turning, until lightly browned all over, about 5 minutes.

Stir in the water, broth, oregano, bay leaf and 1/2 to 3/4 cup of the chile sauce, depending on how much heat you like. Bring to a low boil, then lower to a simmer. Partly cover and cook, turning the pork now and then, until tender, about 3 hours.
Stir in the hominy and simmer uncovered until the pork starts falling apart, about 1 hour more. Remove the bay leaf.
Move the pork to a cutting board, chop it roughly and return it to the pot. Thin with a little water or broth if it's too thick. Taste, and add a pinch of salt substitute only if it needs it.
Serve with the cabbage, radishes, onion, lime and oregano, and the rest of the chile sauce on the side.
notes: Ryan's own recipe, developed from several versions of posole. The chiles de árbol bring serious heat; use fewer for a milder pot. Tastes even better the next day and freezes well for up to 3 months.
heartNotes: Pork tenderloin is one of the leanest cuts there is, and trimming it makes it leaner still. Lightened: the kosher salt (about 1 1/2 teaspoons across the recipe) is gone, the broth is low-sodium, the hominy is rinsed, and one tablespoon of avocado oil replaces two of vegetable oil. A pile of cabbage and radishes on top adds crunch and fiber.

title: Korean Tofu Tacos with Kimchi Slaw
summary: Crispy gochujang-glazed tofu in warm corn tortillas with a quick, creamy kimchi slaw.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons natural peanut butter (no salt or sugar added)
1 tablespoon reduced-sodium tamari, or 2 tablespoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site)
1 teaspoon honey or monk fruit sweetener
2 packages (14 oz each) extra-firm tofu, drained, patted dry and cut into 1/2-inch cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Whisk all the gochujang sauce ingredients together in a medium bowl.
Heat the avocado oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tofu and cook, turning, until crisp in spots, 6 to 8 minutes.
Pour in the gochujang sauce and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until the sauce coats the tofu and turns sticky. Keep going if the tofu still looks wet; you want it crisp.
Toss the coleslaw mix, red cabbage, kimchi, yogurt, mayonnaise, rice vinegar and pepper together in a large bowl.
Wrap the tortillas in foil and warm them in the oven for 4 to 5 minutes.
Fill each tortilla with tofu and kimchi slaw, and top with scallions and parsley.
notes: Gochujang ranges from mild to very hot, so start with a tablespoon if you're unsure. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend. Adapted from Purple Carrot.
heartNotes: Lightened: half as much kimchi, stretched with fresh red cabbage, since kimchi is salty. Reduced-sodium tamari, no added salt, and Greek yogurt with a little light mayo in place of all-mayo dressing. Tofu is a cholesterol-free protein, and corn tortillas are a whole grain.

title: Chili Garlic Pork Noodles
summary: Noodles tossed in a sizzling gochugaru chili oil with garlic, ginger, black vinegar and crumbled pork.
ingredients: 1/2 lb lean ground pork (96% lean) or ground turkey
1 1/2 to 2 tablespoons gochugaru (or red pepper flakes)
4 scallions, whites and greens sliced separately
1 tablespoon reduced-sodium soy sauce, or 2 tablespoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site)
1 teaspoon honey or monk fruit sweetener
2 heads baby bok choy, quartered, or 2 cups baby spinach
steps: Cook the noodles according to the package, without salt. Add the bok choy for the last minute. Drain, saving 1/4 cup of the cooking water.
Meanwhile, brown the pork in a dry nonstick skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it into small crumbles, 5 to 6 minutes. Drain off any fat.
Put the gochugaru, garlic, ginger and scallion whites in a heatproof bowl. Heat the avocado oil in a small pan until it shimmers, then pour it over the bowl. It will sizzle.
Stir the soy sauce, black vinegar and honey into the chili oil.
Toss the noodles, bok choy and pork with the chili oil, adding a splash of the saved cooking water to loosen it. Top with scallion greens and sesame seeds.
notes: Gochugaru is fruity and moderately hot; red pepper flakes are hotter, so start with less. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend. Inspired by Ian Fujimoto's "not a chef" chili oil noodles.
heartNotes: Lightened: half the soy sauce, 2 tablespoons of oil instead of 1/4 cup, 1 teaspoon of honey instead of a tablespoon of sugar, and 96% lean pork drained of its fat. Whole-wheat or soba noodles and bok choy add fiber and greens. Black vinegar brings big flavor with almost no sodium.

title: Avgolemono (Greek Lemon Chicken Soup)
summary: A silky Greek soup of chicken and rice in a bright lemon broth, thickened with a whisked egg.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded cooked chicken breast (about 8 oz)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the broth and bring to a boil. Stir in the rice, lower the heat, and simmer for 16 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk the lemon juice, cornstarch, pepper and egg until smooth.
While whisking the soup constantly, pour in the egg mixture in a thin stream so it thickens the broth without scrambling.
Add the chicken and spinach and cook until the soup thickens slightly and the rice is tender, about 3 minutes. Top with parsley and basil.
notes: Keep whisking as the egg goes in; that's what makes the broth creamy instead of stringy. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: The 1/2 teaspoon of salt is gone and the broth is low-sodium, which cuts the sodium by more than half. Lemon carries the flavor. Lean chicken breast and a single egg keep it light, and the spinach adds greens.

title: Spicy Thai Coconut Chicken Soup
summary: A fragrant lemongrass and ginger soup with chicken, mushrooms and light coconut milk.
ingredients: 1 teaspoon honey or monk fruit sweetener
2 cups shredded cooked chicken breast (about 8 oz)
3 tablespoons chopped fresh parsley or Thai basil
steps: Heat the avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the mushrooms, bell pepper, snap peas, ginger, garlic and lemongrass and cook 3 minutes, stirring now and then.
Stir in the sambal oelek and cook 1 minute.
Add the broth, coconut milk and honey and bring to a simmer. Lower the heat and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the chicken and heat through, about 1 minute. Remove the lemongrass.
Top with green onions, parsley and lime juice.
notes: Start with 1 teaspoon of sambal and add more at the table. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: the 4 teaspoons of fish sauce are gone, the broth is low-sodium, and a teaspoon of honey replaces a tablespoon of sugar. Light coconut milk keeps the saturated fat down, and snap peas add vegetables.

title: Chicken-Udon Soup
summary: Thick udon noodles and chicken in a ginger, star anise and shiitake broth.
ingredients: 6 oz dried udon noodles (whole-wheat if you can find them)
1/4 cup sake, dry sherry or dry white wine
2 cups shredded cooked chicken breast (about 8 oz)
steps: Pull the stems off the mushrooms and save them; slice the caps. Put the stems, broth, ginger slices, crushed garlic, green onion and star anise in a saucepan and bring to a boil. Cover and simmer 20 minutes.
Take the broth off the heat, let it stand 10 minutes, then strain it and discard the solids.
Cook the noodles according to the package, without salt. Drain and rinse with cold water.
Heat the avocado oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the sliced mushroom caps 2 minutes, then the minced ginger and garlic for 1 minute.
Add the sake and cook 4 minutes, scraping up the browned bits. Pour in the strained broth and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and add the chicken, bok choy, soy sauce and honey. Simmer 2 minutes, until the bok choy is tender.
Divide the noodles among 4 bowls, ladle the soup over, and top with green onions.
notes: Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: The kosher salt is gone and the broth is low-sodium, so all the flavor comes from ginger, star anise and mushrooms. Less honey than the original, and bok choy adds greens.

title: Chicken Soup with Cabbage and Apple
summary: A hearty soup with chicken, potatoes, cabbage and tart apple, warmed with toasted caraway and fennel.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded cooked chicken breast (about 8 oz)
steps: Toast the caraway and fennel seeds in a dry skillet over medium heat for 2 minutes, stirring. Grind them in a spice grinder.
Heat the avocado oil in a Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrot, celery and garlic for 6 minutes.
Add the ground chicken and half the ground spices and cook, breaking it up, until no longer pink. Stir in the rest of the spices for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and potatoes and bring to a boil. Cover, lower the heat, and simmer 10 minutes.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the cabbage, shredded chicken, apple, vinegar and pepper, and cook 3 minutes.
notes: The fennel and caraway give the ground chicken a sausage-like flavor without the salt. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: lean ground chicken seasoned with fennel and caraway replaces the processed chicken-apple sausage, the kosher salt is gone, and the broth is low-sodium. Cabbage, apple and potatoes make it filling and high in fiber.

title: Pan-Seared Halibut with Bell Pepper Relish
summary: Golden halibut fillets topped with a warm, smoky bell pepper and tomato relish.
ingredients: 4 wild Alaskan halibut fillets (6 oz each)
Pinch of potassium chloride salt substitute (optional)
steps: Heat 2 1/4 teaspoons of the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Season the halibut with pepper and the salt substitute, if using.
Cook the fish 3 minutes per side, until it flakes easily with a fork. Move it to a plate and keep warm.
Add the rest of the oil to the pan. Cook the shallots and garlic 1 minute.
Add the bell pepper, tomato, vinegar and paprika and cook 3 minutes, until the pepper is tender. Stir in the parsley and spoon the relish over the fish.
notes: Serve with a simple spinach salad. The relish is also good on grilled chicken. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Halibut is a lean, low-fat fish. The salt is now an optional pinch of salt substitute, and sherry vinegar and smoked paprika do the flavor work. Avocado oil keeps the fat unsaturated.

title: Shrimp with Lemon-Saffron Rice
summary: A weeknight take on paella: shrimp, peas and peppers in saffron-scented brown rice.
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper 3 minutes, then the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp and cook 1 to 2 minutes, just until pink. Move the shrimp to a plate.
Add the rice, broth, water, tomato, oregano, saffron, paprika and pepper. Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer until the rice is tender, about 10 minutes.
Stir in the peas and shrimp, cover, and let stand 3 minutes off the heat. Stir in the lemon juice.
notes: Taking the shrimp out while the rice cooks keeps them tender. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: The salt is gone, the broth is low-sodium, and instant brown rice replaces white for more fiber. Shrimp is very low in saturated fat, and the tomato and peas add vegetables.

title: Seafood Cioppino
summary: A San Francisco-style tomato and white wine stew with snapper, scallops, shrimp and clams.
ingredients: 1 can (28 oz) low-sodium whole tomatoes, coarsely chopped, with their juice
10 oz yellowtail snapper fillet, cut into 1-inch pieces
5 oz medium shrimp (about 8), peeled and deveined
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Cook the onion 1 minute, add the garlic, lower the heat to medium, cover, and cook 8 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the wine, broth, basil, oregano, red pepper and tomatoes. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 15 minutes.
Season the snapper and scallops with black pepper. Heat the remaining oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear them 90 seconds per side, until golden.
Add the snapper, scallops, shrimp and clams to the tomato broth. Cover and cook 4 minutes, until the clams open; discard any that stay closed.
Stir in the parsley and lemon juice.
notes: For a side, toast a slice of whole-grain sourdough, rub it with a cut garlic clove and brush lightly with olive oil. Buy dry-packed scallops for the best sear. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: The original used rinsed regular canned tomatoes and boxed broth; low-sodium tomatoes and low-sodium broth cut the biggest sources of sodium. The seafood is lean and naturally rich in omega-3s.

title: Herbed Shrimp and White Bean Salad
summary: Honey-glazed grilled shrimp over arugula, white beans and tomatoes in a sherry-herb vinaigrette.
ingredients: 1 can (15.5 oz) low-sodium Great Northern beans, rinsed and drained
1 lb medium shrimp (about 24), peeled and deveined
steps: Whisk the vinegar, oil, thyme, garlic, rosemary and pepper in a large bowl. Add the arugula, watercress, tomatoes, parsley and beans and toss gently.
Stir the honey and water together in a medium bowl, then toss the shrimp in it.
Heat a grill pan over medium-high heat and coat with cooking spray. Cook the shrimp 2 minutes per side, until done. Serve over the salad.
notes: Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: The salt is gone and the beans are low-sodium, which removes most of the sodium. Beans and greens bring 5 grams of fiber per serving, and the herbs and sherry vinegar carry the flavor.

title: Shrimp Salad Rolls
summary: Tarragon and lemon shrimp salad tucked into toasted whole-wheat buns or crisp lettuce cups.
ingredients: 1 lb large shrimp (about 20), peeled and deveined
4 whole-wheat hot dog buns (or skip the buns and use extra lettuce)
steps: Heat the broiler. Heat the avocado oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp 4 minutes, until done.
Spread the shrimp on a plate and chill 10 minutes, then chop coarsely.
Mix the shrimp with the mayonnaise, yogurt, celery, lemon rind, lemon juice, parsley, tarragon and pepper.
Open the buns without splitting them all the way and toast them cut side up under the broiler for about 1 minute.
Line each bun with 2 lettuce leaves and fill with about 1/2 cup of shrimp salad.
notes: For a lower-carb version, serve the shrimp salad in lettuce cups. Skip the store-bought potato side; roasted fresh potatoes with herbs are better and have no added salt. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: half the mayonnaise is swapped for nonfat Greek yogurt, a teaspoon of oil replaces the butter, the salt is gone, and whole-wheat buns or lettuce replace white buns. Celery adds crunch.

title: Shrimp and Pea Rice Bowl
summary: A 20-minute bowl of garlicky shrimp, peas and spinach over turmeric-tinted brown rice.
ingredients: 1 pouch (8.8 oz) precooked plain brown rice
8 oz medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Heat the rice according to the package.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the shrimp 2 minutes, add the garlic, and cook 1 minute more, until the shrimp are done. Move them to a plate.
Bring the water to a simmer in the pan. Add the peas, cover, and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the rice, shrimp, spinach, vinegar, red pepper and turmeric and cook 1 minute, until the spinach wilts. Top with parsley.
notes: Pick a rice pouch with no added salt; some flavored ones carry a lot of sodium. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: The 3/4 teaspoon of kosher salt was nearly all of the original's sodium, and it's gone. Brown rice, peas and spinach make it a fiber-rich bowl, and vinegar brightens it.

title: Beef Tenderloin Steaks with Balsamic Green Beans
summary: Seared tenderloin steaks with green beans and sweet onions glazed in balsamic vinegar.
ingredients: 4 beef tenderloin steaks (4 oz each), trimmed of visible fat, or 1 lb flank steak
steps: Heat 1 teaspoon of the oil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat. Cook the onions and shallots 6 minutes, then the garlic 1 minute.
Add the broth and cook 4 minutes, until the onions are tender and the liquid is almost gone.
Add the green beans and vinegar, cover, and cook 4 minutes, until crisp-tender. Stir in the remaining teaspoon of oil and keep warm.
Season the steaks with pepper. Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and coat with cooking spray. Cook the steaks 3 minutes per side, or to the doneness you like.
Let the steaks rest 5 minutes, then serve with the green beans.
notes: Flank steak is the budget pick; slice it thinly against the grain. For a side, roast cubed red potatoes with olive oil and fresh thyme instead of the original's packaged mashed potatoes with Parmesan. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: olive oil replaces the butter, the salt is gone, the broth is low-sodium, and the steaks are trimmed. Tenderloin and flank are among the leanest beef cuts, and a 4-ounce portion keeps saturated fat in check.

title: Chicken and Rice with Mushrooms
summary: An earthy one-pan dinner of chicken, brown basmati, peas and two kinds of mushrooms.
ingredients: 1 lb boneless, skinless chicken breast (or trimmed thighs), cut into 1-inch pieces
steps: Pour the boiling water over the porcini and let stand 20 minutes. Strain, saving the soaking liquid, and chop the mushrooms finely.
Heat half the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with paprika and 1/4 teaspoon pepper and cook 5 minutes, until browned. Move it to a plate.
Add the rest of the oil, the onion and the cremini, sprinkle with the remaining pepper, and cook 4 minutes, until lightly browned.
Stir in the porcini liquid, chopped porcini and rice. Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat, and simmer 35 minutes.
Stir in the chicken, peas and thyme. Cover and cook 10 minutes more, until the rice is tender and the chicken is done.
notes: Pour the porcini liquid off slowly and leave the last bit in the bowl; any grit settles there. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Nearly all of the original's 620 mg of sodium came from 3/4 teaspoon of salt, which is gone. Half the oil, chicken breast or trimmed thighs, and brown basmati, peas and mushrooms keep it high in fiber.

title: Honey-Mustard Glazed Chicken
summary: Seared chicken breasts baked under a tangy honey, mustard and thyme glaze.
ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves (6 oz each)
1 tablespoon stone-ground mustard (low-sodium if you can find it)
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Heat the oil in a large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat. Season the chicken with pepper and brown it 2 minutes per side. Move it to a plate.
Add the broth, honey, thyme and garlic to the pan and bring to a boil, scraping up the browned bits. Cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the vinegar and mustard and cook 1 minute. Return the chicken, spoon the sauce over it, and bake 10 minutes, until the chicken reaches 165°F.
Let the chicken rest 5 minutes. Meanwhile, simmer the sauce on the stove for 2 minutes, until syrupy, and spoon it over the chicken.
notes: Also good with skinless chicken thighs or pork tenderloin. Serve with steamed green beans and brown rice. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: 2 tablespoons of honey replace 1/4 cup of maple syrup, the salt is gone, and the broth is low-sodium. Skinless chicken breast is lean, and the mustard and vinegar give the glaze its punch.

title: Tex-Mex Rice Bowl
summary: An 11-minute bowl of seasoned lean beef, black beans, corn and fresh pico over brown rice.
ingredients: 1 pouch (8.8 oz) precooked plain brown rice
1 1/2 tablespoons No-Salt Taco and Fajita Seasoning (from this site)
1 can (15 oz) low-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
1 cup fresh pico de gallo (homemade, no salt)
steps: Heat the rice according to the package.
Brown the beef in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, breaking it up. Drain any fat.
Stir in the water and taco seasoning and bring to a simmer. Add the corn and beans and cook 1 minute, until hot.
Divide the rice and romaine among bowls, top with the beef mixture, pico de gallo, jalapeño and parsley, and serve with lime.
notes: For pico de gallo, mix diced tomato, onion, jalapeño, parsley and lime juice. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: your own No-Salt Taco and Fajita Seasoning replaces the packet, the beans are low-sodium, and the pico is homemade without salt. Lean sirloin, beans and brown rice make it high in protein and fiber, and romaine adds greens.

title: Spicy Turkey and Spinach Rice Bowl
summary: Garlicky ground turkey seasoned like Italian sausage, with spinach and a little Parmesan over brown rice.
ingredients: 1 pouch (8.8 oz) precooked plain brown rice
steps: Heat the rice according to the package.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the turkey, fennel, paprika and red pepper and cook 4 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the garlic and cook 30 seconds, stirring.
Add the spinach and toss until it begins to wilt, about 30 seconds. Stir in the rice and cook 1 minute. Sprinkle with the cheese.
notes: Fennel, paprika and red pepper are what make Italian sausage taste like sausage, without the salt. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: lean ground turkey seasoned with fennel replaces processed hot turkey Italian sausage, which carried most of the sodium, and the Parmesan is cut in half. Spinach and brown rice add fiber.

title: Tomato and Asparagus "Carbonara"
summary: Whole-wheat penne tossed with asparagus, burst cherry tomatoes and a light egg and pecorino sauce.
ingredients: 1 lb asparagus, trimmed and cut diagonally into 1-inch pieces
1 1/2 oz pecorino Romano, finely grated (about 1/3 cup)
steps: Bring the water to a boil in a Dutch oven. Do not add salt.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the asparagus 3 1/2 minutes, add the garlic for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes, until tender.
Whisk the cheese, pepper and egg together in a large bowl.
Cook the pasta 10 minutes, until al dente. Drain and immediately toss the hot pasta with the egg mixture, then add the tomato mixture and toss until the sauce thickens.
Divide among 4 bowls and top with basil.
notes: Toss the pasta with the egg while it's still steaming hot; the heat cooks the egg into a creamy sauce. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: the 1/2 teaspoon of salt is gone, there's a little less pecorino, and whole-wheat penne adds fiber. One egg makes the whole sauce, so there's no cream or bacon.

title: Pasta with Roasted Tomatoes and Garlic
summary: Whole-wheat spaghetti in a glossy olive oil sauce with sweet roasted cherry tomatoes and basil.
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F. Toss the tomatoes and garlic with 2 tablespoons of the oil on a rimmed baking sheet and roast 11 minutes, until they start to burst.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti in a large pot of unsalted boiling water for 10 minutes, until al dente. Drain, saving 6 tablespoons of the cooking water.
Bring the saved water and the remaining tablespoon of oil to a boil in a small saucepan and boil 4 minutes, until reduced to about 1/3 cup.
Toss the pasta with the reduced liquid, roasted tomatoes, pepper and arugula. Top with the cheese and basil.
notes: Boiling the pasta water with the oil makes a light, creamy sauce that clings to the noodles. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: no salt in the pasta water or the sauce (the original used over a tablespoon), a quarter less oil, half the Parmesan, and whole-wheat spaghetti. Arugula adds greens.

title: Black Bean Cakes with Greens and Eggs
summary: Crispy cumin-spiced black bean patties with a lime-dressed salad and a fried egg.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon avocado oil, divided
1 can (15 oz) low-sodium black beans, rinsed and drained
steps: Pulse 1 teaspoon of the avocado oil, 1 egg and the beans in a food processor about 20 times, until coarsely chopped. Stir in 5 tablespoons of the panko, the green onions, parsley, cumin, red pepper and garlic.
Shape into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick and dredge in the remaining panko.
Heat the remaining tablespoon of avocado oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the patties 3 minutes per side and move to a plate.
Wipe the pan, coat it with cooking spray, and crack in the 4 eggs. Cover and cook 4 minutes, or 5 for firmer yolks.
Whisk the olive oil, lime juice, mustard and pepper, and toss with the lettuce. Serve each patty with salad and an egg.
notes: Chilling the patties for 10 minutes before cooking helps them hold together. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: about half the oil (the original used 3 tablespoons of canola plus olive oil), no salt, low-sodium beans, and whole-wheat panko. Beans bring 5 grams of fiber per serving.

title: Red Lentil Dal with Carrot Salad and Flatbreads
summary: Spiced red lentils with spinach, a bright carrot ribbon salad, coriander flatbreads and brown rice.
ingredients: 4 cups shaved carrot (about 2 large, cut with a vegetable peeler)
4 oz refrigerated whole-wheat pizza dough, cut into 4 pieces
steps: Soak the lentils in 3 cups of the water for 20 minutes, then drain.
Heat the oil in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat and cook the onion 3 minutes. Add the ginger, garlic, cumin, garam masala, curry powder and serranos and cook 30 seconds.
Add the lentils and the remaining 2 cups of water, bring to a boil, and simmer 23 minutes. Stir in the spinach and cook 2 minutes, until wilted.
For the salad, whisk the oil, lime rind, lime juice and honey, then toss with the carrot, onion, parsley and mint.

For the flatbreads, roll each piece of dough into a 5-inch round. Heat a grill pan over high heat, coat with cooking spray, and cook the rounds 2 minutes per side, until charred in spots. Sprinkle with coriander.
Serve the dal over brown rice with the salad and flatbreads.
notes: Ground coriander is the dried seed and tastes warm and citrusy. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: the salt is gone (over a teaspoon in the original), half the oil in the salad, honey instead of sugar, and whole-wheat dough. Lentils, spinach, carrots and brown rice give each plate about 11 grams of fiber.

title: Grilled Sweet Potato and Napa Cabbage Salad with Lime Vinaigrette
summary: Smoky grilled sweet potato strips tossed with crunchy napa cabbage, pumpkin seeds and a honey-lime dressing.
steps: Set up the grill for indirect heat: one side medium-high, the other side off.
Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them lengthwise into 1/2-inch slices. Toss with 1 tablespoon of the oil and 1/4 teaspoon pepper.
Grill the slices on the unheated side, lid closed, 12 minutes per side, until tender. Move them to the hot side and grill 2 minutes per side, until charred.
Whisk the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil and 1/4 teaspoon pepper with the lime juice, water, honey and jalapeño in a large bowl.
Cut the sweet potatoes into strips and add them to the bowl with the cabbage, red onion, pumpkin seeds, green onions and parsley. Toss.
notes: No grill? Roast the sweet potato slices at 425°F for 25 minutes, turning once. Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry skillet. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: 3 tablespoons of oil instead of 5, no salt (the original used 3/4 teaspoon), and unsalted pumpkin seeds. Sweet potatoes and cabbage bring nearly 6 grams of fiber per serving.

title: Cider-Glazed Carrots
summary: Whole baby carrots glazed in a tangy reduction of cider vinegar and honey.
ingredients: 2 lb baby carrots with tops, trimmed but not peeled
Pinch of potassium chloride salt substitute (optional)
steps: Cook the carrots in boiling water for 5 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water, and rub off the skins with a clean towel. Pat dry.
Bring the vinegar and honey to a boil in a medium skillet and cook 6 minutes, until reduced to about 1/4 cup.
Add the carrots, turn the heat to high, and cook 2 minutes, until the glaze is syrupy and coats them.
Stir in the olive oil and the salt substitute, if using.
notes: Multicolored baby carrots look great here. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: olive oil replaces the butter, honey replaces brown sugar, and the salt is now an optional pinch of salt substitute.

title: Wild Rice with Carrots
summary: Nutty wild rice with tender sautéed carrots and parsley, plus three easy swaps.
ingredients: 1 package (8.5 oz) precooked wild rice, or 2 cups cooked wild rice
steps: Heat the rice according to the package.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the carrot 8 minutes, stirring often, until tender.
Stir in the rice, parsley and pepper and cook 1 minute.
notes:
If you can't find precooked wild rice, use precooked brown rice.
Swap the carrots for one of these:
- Bell pepper and fennel: Cook 1/2 cup each diced yellow bell pepper and fennel in the oil instead of the carrot. Finish with 1 1/2 teaspoons chopped fresh oregano.
- Cucumber and feta (no cooking): Toss the warm rice with 1 cup diced English cucumber, 1 1/2 tablespoons olive oil, 1 tablespoon lemon juice and 1 oz crumbled feta.
- Tomatoes and pine nuts: Cook 1/4 cup pine nuts and 8 quartered cherry tomatoes in the oil for 8 minutes, then stir in the rice and 1 tablespoon chopped basil.
Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: olive oil replaces the butter and the salt is gone in every version. The feta version uses half the original cheese. Wild rice is a whole grain with more protein than most.

title: Napa Cabbage Slaw
summary: A crisp, gingery Asian-style slaw of napa cabbage, squash and carrot, with apple for a sweet crunch.
ingredients: 1 tablespoon reduced-sodium soy sauce, or 2 tablespoons Low-Sodium Soy Sauce Substitute (from this site)
1/2 teaspoon gochugaru (Korean red pepper flakes), or crushed red pepper
1 small apple (Honeycrisp or Fuji), cut into matchsticks
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, sesame oil, vinegar, honey, ginger and gochugaru in a large bowl.
Add the vegetables and apple, toss well, and let stand 10 minutes before serving.
notes:
Shortcut: use 3 cups of a premixed bag of shredded cabbage or coleslaw mix in place of the napa cabbage, red cabbage and carrot.
Gochugaru brings a fruity, smoky heat that's milder than crushed red pepper. Find it in the Asian aisle or at Korean markets.
Toss the apple in right before serving so it stays crisp. Great with the Spicy Bulgogi (Pork, Beef or Chicken) or alongside grilled fish. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: honey and gochugaru replace bottled sweet chili sauce, which is mostly sugar, and there's a little less sesame oil. Red cabbage adds color and fiber.

title: Corn Chowchow
summary: A tangy, lightly sweet relish of fresh corn, peppers, green tomato and tomatillo.
ingredients: 1 cup champagne vinegar or white wine vinegar
steps: Bring the vinegar, honey, water, peppercorns and bay leaf to a boil in a medium saucepan.
Add the corn and the rest of the vegetables and simmer 15 minutes.
Remove the bay leaf. Serve the chowchow chilled or at room temperature.
notes: Seed the jalapeño for a milder relish. Spoon it over grilled chicken, fish or pork. Keeps a week in the fridge. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: 2 tablespoons of honey replace 1/2 cup of sugar, and the salt is gone. It's a fat-free way to add big flavor to lean proteins.

title: Tzatziki
summary: A cool Greek yogurt sauce with grated cucumber, dill and garlic.
ingredients: 1/4 cup grated peeled English cucumber, squeezed dry
steps: Stir everything together in a medium bowl. Chill until ready to serve.
notes: Use garlic without green sprouts inside, which taste bitter. Serve with chicken or beef kebabs, burgers, pita sandwiches or raw vegetables. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: nonfat Greek yogurt instead of low-fat, no salt, and a little lemon rind to brighten it. About 35 calories per 3-tablespoon serving.

title: Mushroom Sauce
summary: A savory sautéed mushroom and white wine pan sauce for steak, chicken or pork.
steps: Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat and coat it with cooking spray. Cook the mushrooms and shallot 6 minutes, until browned and the liquid is gone. Stir in the thyme.
Whisk the broth, wine, cornstarch and pepper together and add to the pan. Bring to a boil and cook 1 minute, until thickened.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the olive oil.
notes: Let the sauce bubble so the cornstarch thickens it. Great with steak, roasted chicken or pork, or over brown rice. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: a tablespoon of olive oil replaces 2 tablespoons of butter, the salt is gone, and the broth is low-sodium. A shallot adds depth.

title: Chocolate Chip-Coffee Muffins
summary: Tender mocha muffins with a little dark chocolate, for an occasional breakfast treat.
ingredients: 1/3 cup monk fruit and allulose blend
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F.
Stir the milk, oil, coffee granules, vanilla and egg together until the coffee dissolves.
Whisk the flours, sugar, monk fruit blend, chocolate chips and baking powder in a large bowl. Make a well in the center, pour in the milk mixture, and stir just until moist.
Spoon the batter into 12 muffin cups coated with cooking spray. Bake 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Remove from the pan right away and cool on a rack.
notes: A treat, not an everyday breakfast. Monk fruit tip: many monk fruit sweeteners are blended with erythritol. Check the label and pick pure monk fruit or a monk fruit and allulose blend. Adapted from Cooking Light.
heartNotes: Lightened: avocado oil replaces 5 tablespoons of butter (cutting saturated fat by about two-thirds), nonfat milk replaces whole, half the flour is whole wheat, half the sugar is swapped for monk fruit and allulose, there are fewer chocolate chips, and the salt is gone.
